scenes.say: Should you cache or persist your DataFrame in Spark? Let’s see why this choice matters.

scenes.label: Memory
scenes.sub: Stores DataFrame in RAM for fast reuse.
scenes.say: Caching puts your DataFrame in memory, so repeated operations run much faster.

scenes.title: Disk Storage
lines: DataFrame stored on disk, not RAM
scenes.say: Persistence can store data on disk instead of memory. This saves RAM but is slower.
Cache only when a DataFrame is reused. Always monitor memory usage to avoid spilling. Don’t cache everything.

scenes.question: Should you always cache DataFrames?
scenes.right: No. Cache only reused DataFrames and monitor memory.
scenes.say: Interview trap: Should you always cache? No. Cache only reused DataFrames and keep an eye on memory.
